evidence_against: The bearish/late-cycle interpretation is not coherently confirmed by price: BTC and ETH returns are positive across usable 4h, 12h, 24h, and 72h windows, while the 1h horizon has a 0.0-hour actual span and is non-informative.

Breadth improved between live-anchor captures from 68 to 70 advancers and from 27 to 25 decliners. This is proxy-only evidence with changing point-in-time membership, but it contradicts a contemporaneous claim of clearly deteriorating participation.

ETH/BTC is below its 4h, 12h, 24h, and 72h anchors (-0.13%, -0.22%, -0.35%, and -0.94%), but direct hourly closes remain above 0.0300 for all 168 retained observations. Recent relative weakness therefore does not by itself establish a structural breakdown.

The 24h and 72h derivative readings do not uniformly corroborate deleveraging: BTC/ETH open interest increased over 24h, and ETH open interest increased 6.44% over 72h, despite falling over 4h and 12h.
Recent short-liquidation observations are post-cutoff and lower-bound, source-fragile aggregates. They cannot serve as contemporaneous confirmation of either exhaustion or durable upside.
evidence_for: A coherent deterioration-risk reading exists in the repeated divergence: BTC and ETH rose across usable horizons while ETH/BTC fell across every usable reported horizon, indicating weaker ETH relative performance during the advance.

At 4h and 12h, BTC and ETH prices advanced while both open-interest measures declined and long/short changes were negative. BTC net aggressive quote flow was negative over 12h and 24h, despite positive BTC returns.

The 72h horizon extends the relative-weakness pattern: BTC returned 1.82%, ETH returned 0.90%, and ETH/BTC returned -0.94%; BTC open interest declined 0.57% and net aggressive quote flow was negative.

Rotation proxies do not show confirmed broad-alt acceleration: BlockchainCenter 30-day and 90-day scores are 67 and 59, and CoinMarketCap's 90-day score is 60; all are between their published thresholds and are shadow context only.
The conflict router identifies multi-horizon disagreement between positive BTC/ETH returns and negative derivative/relative-strength metrics at 4h, 12h, 24h, and 72h.
hypotheses: Strongest coherent interpretation: the supplied snapshot is an advancing absolute-price move with fragile or incomplete transmission. Positive BTC/ETH returns, modestly improving proxy breadth, and positive but modest funding coexist with weakening ETH/BTC and mixed leverage/flow evidence. This supports neither confirmed broad-alt acceleration nor a confirmed late-cycle deterioration label.

Strongest falsification of premature late-cycle bearishness: sustained positive BTC/ETH returns across 4h-72h, improved live-anchor proxy breadth, and ETH/BTC persistence above 0.0300 are inconsistent with declaring an already-established broad breakdown from relative weakness and selected short-horizon derivative declines alone.

Strongest falsification of delayed recognition of genuine deterioration: the repeated ETH/BTC losses across all usable horizons, negative BTC aggressive flow over 12h and 24h, and 4h/12h open-interest contraction may be early evidence that the absolute-price advance lacks durable relative and positioning confirmation. Treating price strength alone as sufficient would disregard this repeated divergence.

The appropriate conflict interpretation remains descriptive: possible early transmission deterioration is present, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether it will resolve through renewed ETH/breadth confirmation or through a pullback.
summary: Detected conflict is persistent rather than isolated: absolute BTC and ETH performance is positive across usable horizons, whereas ETH/BTC is negative across each usable horizon and derivative/flow signals are mixed to negative in key short windows. The strongest coherent reading is an advancing market with weakened relative transmission, not a ratified late-cycle deterioration. Premature bearishness is challenged by positive multi-horizon returns, improving proxy breadth, and sustained ETH/BTC closes above 0.0300; delayed recognition is challenged by repeated ETH/BTC underperformance, negative BTC flow at 12h/24h, and recent open-interest contraction. This is a shadow-only conflict interpretation.
uncertainties: The 1h horizon has a 0.0-hour actual span; its zero changes provide no directional evidence.
Breadth is noncanonical proxy-only evidence and point-in-time membership differs between captures, limiting direct comparability.
ETH/BTC persistence above 0.0300 measures level persistence, not recent relative-return improvement.
Open-interest and long/short changes disagree by horizon; 24h and 72h do not uniformly support a deleveraging narrative.
Macro and legacy spot data are unavailable. ETF context is a dated October 2 settled session and is mixed: BTC +31.7, ETH -17.3.
Post-cutoff Pullback Forensics and rich-breadth observations are excluded from cutoff-time confirmation; liquidation aggregates are lower bounds from a fragile legacy source.
No supplied evidence establishes the timing, magnitude, or probability of a pullback, continuation, or structural cycle transition.
